reason: This passage (Exodus 1:6-12) describes the oppression of the Hebrew people by Egyptian taskmasters but contains no account of the Israelites themselves voicing any criticism. The only speech recorded in this fragment is from the new Pharaoh expressing concern to his Egyptian people about the Israelite population. While the passage depicts the Israelites being afflicted and forced to build cities, it does not document any complaint, murmuring, or criticism directed by the Hebrew people against either their leaders or Yahweh.
